newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends lower, reverting to bearish mode.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends lower, reverting to bearish mode.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended lower Wednesday after bullish oil inventory data failed to extend early session gains, allowing the oil market to slip back into a bearish mode.

"There was an API reversal that has been typical in the past couple weeks, so we are back to seeing lower lows made in late session, which indicates how bearish the market is," said Sal Gugliara of United Energy in New York.
May crude ended off eight cents to $19.27 a barrel after rising as high as $19.77. Spot crude has lost more than $7.00 a barrel since early January on rising crude supplies.

After positive crude settlements Monday and Tuesday, traders had thought crude may be entering an uptrend typically seen in the spring when gasoline rises in anticipation of the summer driving season.
May gasoline rose as much as 0.93 cent Wednesday before settling off 0.47 cent at 60.70 cents a gallon. May heat bucked declines, ending up 0.22 cent at 53.11 cents a gallon.

On Tuesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said the year-over-year gasoline stock deficit had widened to 5.8 million barrels for the week ended April 4 from 5.4 million barrels the week before.
Sometimes oil prices will rise Wednesday morning following the weekly data if its bullish and then fall on profit-taking, dubbed an "API fade" or an "API reversal" which was seen Wednesday.

Countering the API news, IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said Wednesday that all its oil pipelines stretching from western Canada to Ontario and the U.S. Midwest had resumed pumping after a power outage Monday had curtailed one million barrel per day in throughput.
IPL said the system was moving about 1.15 million barrels per day, up from 860,000 late Tuesday.
Dealers said nearby heating oil rose on the back of increasing U.S. Gulf cash values and unseasonably cold weather in the U.S. Northeast.
The National Weather Service said it expects temperatures to remain below normal in the region for the next six to 10 days starting April 13.
The northeastern United States is the largest heating oil market in the world.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
